Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options to avoid price increase

Hi Sean,

Our annual renewal for the Dedicated cluster is coming up in September and our finance team is flagging potential rate increases across our vendor stack. We really value Redwood's latency and consistency, but we need a path to lock unit economics for the next 12–24 months.

Can you share options for multiyear commitments or an advance-deposit structure that: 
- caps price increases or holds current rates,
- gives us a predictable ramp of capacity, and
- provides credits or throttles if we underutilize?

High level: we're considering either a 1-year prepaid with top-up credits or a 2-year advance deposit that amortizes monthly. We're leaning toward protecting our costs while retaining flexibility in our first-quarter scale.

Appreciate a short proposal that we can show procurement. Procurement will want amortization and cancellation terms.

Thanks,
Kellan
VP Product, SculptAI

Kellan O'Neill
SculptAI

Hi Kellan — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a short framework below and attached a one‑page term sheet (Advance-Commitment-Term-Sheet.pdf) for procurement. High level options we can operationalize quickly: 

1) 12-month advance deposit (credit bank)
   - Pay for 12 months upfront at current committed rates.
   - Unused monthly credits roll forward for up to 6 months; beyond that we offer a 50% refund of unused credits.
   - 30% discount off list for committed compute units at current rates.

2) 24-month amortized advance commitment (rate cap) — recommended
   - Customer prepays 50% up front, balance amortized monthly on invoices; effective rate is capped at current pricing for 24 months.
   - Ramp schedule: Year 1 target 60% of committed capacity, Year 2 target 100% (we include staged credit releases if you hit early usage milestones).
   - Early termination: prorated refund less a 6% admin fee; option to convert remaining credit to hosted API at a lower footprint.

3) Hybrid laddered credits + capacity guarantee
   - Laddered discounts as you cross usage tiers; includes a spike buffer for seasonal bursts.

Operational notes: SLA & capacity guarantees included for Dedicated clusters; we can add a capacity 'burst pool' for predictable monthly overage at a fixed uplift. I attached a draft MAP (mutual action plan) to map milestones and procurement items.

If this looks good, Marissa and I will work with finance to produce an amortization schedule and DocuSign-ready SOW. Do you have a preferred legal review timeline?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Advance-Commitment-Term-Sheet.pdf, Draft-MAP.pdf
